findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hard-coded empty data when feature flag is on
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object (`data: []`, `meta: { fields: {}, units: {} }`). The actual result data (`result.data`, `result.meta`), `fields`, `getFieldHeaderMap`, `getCustomFieldRenderer`, and `minTableColumnWidth` are all available in the surrounding scope but are not forwarded. Any organization with the feature flag enabled will see fully empty tables in every dashboard widget, which is a functional regression vs. the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart` branch.

findings.title: Object.keys on possibly undefined meta throws TypeError
findings.body: The fallback column extraction does `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields).map(...)`. Optional chaining on the `?.` only protects `tableData`; if `tableData.meta` is undefined (e.g. when called with `{data: []}` and no `meta`), this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fields')`. The type says `meta` is always present, but the chart.tsx integration actually passes a hard-coded tableData whose meta is present in this PR but the contract is not enforced at runtime. Should be `Object.keys(tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {})` or equivalent.

findings.title: Bare `except Exception` logged at INFO swallows real errors in get_environment_info
findings.body: `CommitContextIntegration.get_environment_info` wraps the whole body in `except Exception as e:` and then logs at INFO level (`logger.info("get_environment_info.no-environment", extra={"issue_id": issue.id, "error": e})`). Catching the bare `Exception` base class will silently swallow programming errors, `DatabaseError`, `ObjectDoesNotExist`, etc., and logging them at INFO hides them from alerting/dashboards. Should narrow to the specific exceptions that are expected (e.g. `Group.DoesNotExist`, `Environment.DoesNotExist`) and log unexpected exceptions at `WARNING` or `EXCEPTION`.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before feature-flag check, polluting analytics with disabled usage
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is invoked on every request, before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)` check that returns 404 for orgs without the flag enabled. This will record an analytics event for every caller — including unauthorized clients and orgs without the feature — biasing usage metrics. The recording should be moved after the feature flag check (and ideally after successful validation) so it only reflects real usage of the endpoint.

findings.title: Analytics event registration relies on side-effect import that may not run before endpoint usage
findings.body: `src/sentry/preprod/__init__.py` does `from .analytics import *` purely for the side effect of `analytics.register(PreprodArtifactApiAssembleEvent)`. The endpoint `organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py` only imports from `sentry.preprod.tasks`, not from `sentry.preprod`. If nothing else imports the `sentry.preprod` package during process startup, the event class will never be registered and `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` may fail or be dropped. There is no Django AppConfig / `ready()` hook in the PR to guarantee registration. Either register the event at module import inside `analytics.py` (it already self-registers) and ensure the package is imported, or add an explicit `default_app_config` so `preprod.apps.PreprodConfig.ready()` runs the registration.

findings.title: Migrations 0917/0920 neutered to no-ops with no test coverage for the deferred migration
findings.body: Both `0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` and `0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py` were reduced to `return` with a comment pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`. The corresponding test `tests/sentry/migrations/test_0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` was deleted in the same PR, and there is no test for `0920`. If `0921` does not exist in the repo, or if it fails to migrate the `SavedSearch -> GroupSearchView` rows correctly, the saved-search-to-view conversion that this migration sequence was supposed to perform will not happen on any environment that runs migrations sequentially — and there is no test guarding against the wrong file being referenced. Verify that 0921 exists and add a migration test (or `TestMigrations`) that exercises the full path the comment references.

findings.title: Migration references non-existent file name in docstring
findings.body: The migration docstring says `See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration.` but no file with that name appears in the PR or in `src/sentry/migrations/` paths shown. If the intended successor migration is `0921_*` with a different suffix, both migration docstrings are wrong and a future engineer will look for a file that does not exist. Verify the correct migration name and fix the docstring, or add the referenced migration if it really is missing.

findings.title: Dead `_handle_regex_match` left behind in parametrize_w_experiments
findings.body: After removing `ParameterizationRegexExperiment`, the inner function `_handle_regex_match` inside `parametrize_w_experiments` (lines ~335-343) is no longer called from the for-loop (which now unconditionally calls `experiment.run(content, _incr_counter)`). The unused closure is dead code, but it still holds a reference and is misleading to future readers who may think experiments can be regex-based.

findings.title: Renamed analytics event `replay.view_html` -> `replay.view-html` is a silent breaking change
findings.body: `trackAnalytics('replay.view_html', ...)` was changed to `trackAnalytics('replay.view-html', ...)`. The corresponding entry in `static/app/utils/analytics/replayAnalyticsEvents.tsx` was updated and the old `replay.view_html` key was removed entirely from `ReplayEventParameters` and `replayEventMap`. Any external dashboard, alert, or query filtering on the literal `replay.view_html` event name will silently stop receiving data. The PR description does not call this out; the rename should be flagged in changelog / product docs, or the old key should be kept as an alias for at least one release.

findings.title: Removed `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` option not asserted by tests
findings.body: The `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` option was deleted from `src/sentry/options/defaults.py`. There are no tests in the PR asserting that no code reads this option key, and `tests/sentry/grouping/test_parameterization.py` continues to test traceparent parameterization behavior. If any deployed instance still has the option persisted in DB / Redis from before this removal, lookups for it will now fail validation when callers pass an unrecognized key — worth grepping for any remaining `options.get("grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent")` references and adding a deprecation removal test.

findings.title: PR description "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System" does not match the diff contents
findings.body: The PR title and description focus on a replays bulk-delete system, but the diff includes large, unrelated changes to grouping parameterization, browser reporting collector, GitHub/GitLab PR templates, autofix defaults, dashboards table widget, explore Visualize refactor (yAxes -> yAxis), feedback AI summaries, integrations, and two migrations that are turned into no-ops. None of these are described in the description. This makes the PR very hard to review and reason about; either split into focused PRs or update the description to enumerate the actual change set so reviewers know what they are signing off on.

findings.title: No test covers the new `use-table-widget-visualization` branch in chart.tsx
findings.body: There is a `tableWidgetVisualization.spec.tsx` testing the new component in isolation, but there is no test exercising the wiring in `chart.tsx` that chooses `TableWidgetVisualization` when the feature flag is on. Given the bug above (empty hard-coded data), this integration test would have caught it. Add an APITestCase / jest test that asserts the new component is rendered with the actual `result.data` / `result.meta` when the flag is on.
